extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in American political theory, national policy, and democratic reform
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts normative criteria for organizing national life so that democracy and nationality reinforce one another — covering centralization, distribution of functions, legitimacy of popular sovereignty, national defense, and remedies for economic contradictions that threaten cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: National defense as prerequisite for peace
rubrics_metrics.description: "The pacific Powers... must keep as well armed as their more belligerent neighbors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that nations desiring peace must maintain sufficient military efficiency; a partial diminution of military capacity by pacific powers would encourage aggressive states. Security and national integrity depend on being as well armed as resources and policy demand; preparedness is a necessary condition for obtaining more to gain from peace than from military victory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual democratic transformation respectful of tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Democratic change must proceed gradually without suddenly uprooting historical traditions and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author emphasizes that national cohesion depends on fidelity to traditional ideas and that abrupt or violent attempts to remove historical institutions (e.g., slavery) carry severe penalties; reforms require fair notice, full discussion, demonstrable need, and sufficient public consent. Nationalization should permit gradual alteration in the direction of increasing democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationalization is not equivalent to mere centralization
rubrics_metrics.description: "The nationalizing of American political, economic, and social life means something more than Federal centralization and something very different therefrom."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization is only one possible means to achieve a coordinated national life; nationalization is a formative transformation aligning organization and policy with a people's needs and ideals. Each instance of centralization must be justified by its fruits; there is no presumption for or against it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional allocation of governmental powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Political power should be distributed among central, state, and municipal officials so it can be efficiently and responsibly exerted in the interest of those affected by its action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions belong to the level of government best able to perform them adequately. The states should retain functions they can perform within limits of efficiency; functions they cannot be expected to perform (e.g., regulation of commerce, organization of labor, control over property in the public interest) should be nationalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for altering constitutional arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a given function should be exercised by the central government in a Federal system is a matter of expediency—with the burden of proof resting on those who propose to alter any existing Constitutional arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to shift powers must demonstrate practical necessity and benefit; appeals to abstract theory or mere hostility to 'states' rights' are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate centralization by demonstrable efficiency and national welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralization must be justified by its fruits; there is no general presumption in its favor or against it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers should assess whether central authority will better serve national economic, social, and moral needs. Centralization is valid when it remedies abuses or enables national coordination that states cannot achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose special-interest capture of national institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies or institutions are not national merely because they are Federal; their national character depends on whether they serve the national welfare rather than special interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal government itself has been 'perverted to the service of special interests' (examples: military pensions, tariff schedules, Sherman Anti-Trust law as presently applied). Assess policy by analyzing beneficiaries and whether public interest is genuinely advanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: National principle as a demand for reform and reconstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The national principle becomes a principle of reform and reconstruction when national consistency demands solutions to contradictory economic and political tendencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National policy should remove obstacles created by economic development (e.g., irresponsible money-power, corporate aggrandizement, class antagonisms) that obstruct democratic fulfillment. The nation's cohesion requires addressing these contradictions before another rupturing crisis occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and powers justified by functional adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: "All rights under the law are functions in a democratic political organism and must be justified by their actual or presumable functional adequacy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal or customary rights should not be defended solely because they are traditional; they must be evaluated for whether they serve democratic and national purposes. If they do not, they should be modified or superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit local government activity to capacities of efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The best friends of local government seek to have its activity confined within limits of possible efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and municipalities should undertake only those functions they can reasonably perform well; confining local roles to achievable tasks preserves their usefulness within an efficient national organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central responsibilities needed by industrialized, centralized activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A more scrupulous attention to existing Federal responsibilities, and the increase of their number and scope, is the natural consequence of the increasing concentration of American industrial, political, and social life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because American activity is becoming more centralized in practice (large corporations, nationwide markets, class divisions), certain responsibilities (e.g., commerce regulation, labor organization, property control) must be exercised at the national level for effective, coherent policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: National democracy must prove its right to advance
rubrics_metrics.description: An American national democracy must always prove its right to a further advance... by the development of a policy and method adequate for the particular occasion, and by its ability to overcome the inevitable opposition of selfish interests and erroneous ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progressive national measures require concrete, practicable plans and political capacity to confront vested interests and misleading traditions. Legitimacy and sustainability depend on demonstrable effectiveness and public persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Popular sovereignty requires collective purpose and national unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The people are Sovereign only in so far as they succeed in reaching and expressing a collective purpose... They are Sovereign in so far as they are united in spirit and in purpose; and they are united in so far as they are loyal one to another, to their joint past, and to the Promise of their future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority rule is a necessary means but not a sufficient source of moral or national authority. The legitimacy of democratic decisions depends on fuller national cohesion, traditions, and deliberate formation of a collective will rather than ephemeral majorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superstitious reverence for constitutional forms
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a strong... tendency to regard the existing Constitution with superstitious awe, and to shrink with horror from modifying it even in the smallest detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal forms should not be worshipped for their own sake; constitutional and legal change is legitimate when required to align national political organization constructively with democratic purposes. Reform should not be obstructed by mere precedent if it thwarts national opportunity and responsibility.
